reviewed_by: Delegated coding agent static review against live Binary Ninja 6.0.10601 MCP (retail PE view_1), radare2 6.2.0 CFG and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast on retail igi.exe; candidate source read from this worktree. No game process was executed and no runtime behavior is claimed.
review_basis: Retail 0x00403A00 was re-disassembled, re-decompiled and re-CFG'd through the live Binary Ninja view, independently recovered with radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast. The candidate is scripts/GameNatives/go/00403A00-GOGameLang.cpp at sha256 8973061e39cd217b50301b295e6157a679b9196d892fcffc11df6532e8f0debf (recorded implementation.signature: int32_t GOGameLang(int32_t param_1, float param_2);). The evidence artifact digests are bound in this review.

checks.name: abi_and_signature
checks.detail: Retail frame slot [E+0xc]; BN (int32_t arg1, float arg2 @ 0xc); candidate's param_2 is [E+8].The retail frame slot is [E+0xc] (BN already models it as arg2/arg3 with an explicit @ 0xc offset). The candidate declaration puts its second (or third) parameter at [E+8], the registered argc slot, so the same source compiled into the QVM call site would read the wrong stack word.

signature_comparison.rationale: Binary Ninja reports "int32_t(int32_t arg1, float arg2 @ 0xc)" at 0x00403A00; radare2 recovers "fcn.00403a00 (int32_t arg_24h, int32_t arg_2ch);". Both tools place the entry at 0x00403A00 and agree on the stack/register word count and cleanup; the difference is the level of type/argument-name detail, not the call frame.
